# Limits and caches

> Pending: Java names follow PR #63 (branch claude/java-api-alignment): the Java names are the aligned API. main still has the earlier names.

Every resource a dataset can make the reader use is bounded by a setting you choose when you open the dataset.
A **limit** fails the operation that exceeds it with a limit error: Go `*LimitError`, which wraps `ErrLimitExceeded`, or Java `LimitExceededException`.
A **cache budget** never fails an operation; past it, the reader stops keeping what it loads.
Exceeding a limit is a policy of yours or a capacity of the reader, never a refusal of the data ([CHECK-5](../../spec/format-1.md#check-5)).
A zero setting takes its default; a negative setting is an invalid request when the dataset is opened.

What to do when an operation exceeds one: [troubleshooting](../guides/troubleshooting.md#limits).

## Settings

Go sets them in `Limits`; Java with `Limits.Builder` methods of the same names.

| Go field | Java method | Default | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`ManifestBytes`](#manifestbytes) | `manifestBytes` | 64 MiB | limit |
| [`Parts`](#parts) | `parts` | 1,000,000 | limit |
| [`FooterBytes`](#footerbytes) | `footerBytes` | 16 MiB | limit |
| [`PageIndexBytes`](#pageindexbytes) | `pageIndexBytes` | 16 MiB | limit |
| [`MetadataMemory`](#metadatamemory) | `metadataMemory` | 256 MiB | limit |
| [`PageBytes`](#pagebytes) | `pageBytes` | 64 MiB | limit |
| [`PageValues`](#pagevalues) | `pageValues` | 16,777,216 | limit |
| [`PageMemory`](#pagememory) | `pageMemory` | 2 × 24 × `PageValues` + `PageBytes`: 832 MiB at their defaults | limit |
| [`IndexMemory`](#indexmemory) | `indexMemory` | 1 GiB | limit |
| [`OffsetIndexMemory`](#offsetindexmemory) | `offsetIndexMemory` | 256 MiB | cache budget |
| [`GetRows`](#getrows) | `getRows` | 1,000 | limit |

## Fixed capacities

These are capacities of the reader, not settings. Exceeding one is reported like a limit.

| Go `LimitName` | Java `LimitName` | Capacity |
|---|---|---|
| `LimitManifestNesting` | `MANIFEST_NESTING` | 512 nested JSON objects and arrays, the manifest object counting 1 |
| `LimitDatasetRows` | `DATASET_ROWS` | a dataset row total of 2^63-1 |

## Each setting

The text below is the Go field comment; the Java method's Javadoc says the same of Java.

### `ManifestBytes`

ManifestBytes bounds the manifest's size. Default 64 MiB.

### `Parts`

Parts bounds the number of parts in a manifest. Default 1,000,000.

### `FooterBytes`

FooterBytes bounds the encoded size of one part's footer. Default 16 MiB.

### `PageIndexBytes`

PageIndexBytes bounds the encoded size of one key column chunk's ColumnIndex, and of its OffsetIndex. Default 16 MiB.

### `MetadataMemory`

MetadataMemory bounds the estimated decoded size of one footer, page index or page header. Default 256 MiB.

### `PageBytes`

PageBytes bounds a page's compressed and uncompressed sizes, and the size of its decoded values' bytes, dictionary pages included. Default 64 MiB. It does not bound the memory of decoding a page: each decoded value page also holds a parquet.Value per value (24 bytes on 64-bit platforms), which PageMemory bounds. Key pages are decoded into their bytes with a 4-byte offset or dictionary index per key.

### `PageValues`

PageValues bounds the number of values in one page or dictionary. Default 16,777,216. Each request retains projected data-page scratch at its high-water capacity until the call ends. Besides PageBytes, header buffers can retain up to headerBytes (16 MiB, bounded by MetadataMemory); indexed raw extents include header and payload. IndexMemory does not account for any of it.

### `PageMemory`

PageMemory bounds the memory decoding one page holds, data and dictionary pages alike, key pages included, estimated from the page's header before anything is allocated for its values (pageMemory): 24 bytes per value for its parquet.Value (64-bit platforms), twice that for an optional column (its non-null values, then every row), plus the bytes its decoded values hold, at most PageBytes. A key page is estimated the same way, though it holds a 4-byte offset or index per key instead of a parquet.Value: the estimate is conservative for it. A page over it fails with an error wrapping ErrLimitExceeded, naming PageMemory. It bounds one page's decoding, not a call's total memory or the high-water scratch a call retains.

Default: the most PageValues and PageBytes allow, 2 × 24 × PageValues + PageBytes, so that the default refuses no page those limits admit: 832 MiB at their defaults. Set it lower to bound decoding memory; a page within PageValues and PageBytes may then be refused. The bound is per page and per request: concurrent requests, and the shards of a split plan scanned at once, each decode their own pages, so their memory adds up; bound concurrency as well.

### `IndexMemory`

IndexMemory bounds the memory one Dataset retains for key page indexes and decoded row-group first-key bytes, which it keeps once loaded. This accounts for page entries and their bound bytes, plus first-key bytes; not allocator overhead, footers, transient decoding buffers or query results. Default 1 GiB.

### `OffsetIndexMemory`

OffsetIndexMemory bounds the memory one Dataset retains for the checked page locations of projected column chunks' OffsetIndexes, which it keeps once loaded so that later requests do not read and decode them again. It is a cache, not a limit on reads: past it, each request loads the locations it needs and drops them, as if no cache were kept, and never with ErrLimitExceeded. It counts page entries plus a fixed per-chunk overhead, apart from IndexMemory. It does not count allocator overhead, the locations a request loads without keeping (including concurrent first loads of one chunk, all but one of which are dropped), or the cache's slots: every opened part allocates about 24 bytes per physical row group and 8 per column chunk on 64-bit platforms when it is checked, whatever the budget and even if no request projects a value column. Default 256 MiB.

### `GetRows`

GetRows bounds the rows Dataset.Get returns: a group of more rows fails with a *LimitError naming GetRows, and is read by paging KeySpan(key) with Rows instead. It bounds a convenience call's row count, not its memory: a few rows can hold large keys and values. Default 1,000.
